oneclickpostfactory.label: OneClickPostFactory
oneclickpostfactory.claim_boundary: Product/workflow framing only; no claim that product-generated copy or every provider is live.
oneclickpostfactory.default_cta: Where does your publishing workflow usually break?

inventory.title: Source material should not die once
inventory.hook: A useful answer should not become disposable content.
inventory.body: The better workflow keeps the source, extracts a useful angle, adapts it to the destination and records what actually published.
inventory.cta: What useful source are you currently leaving unused?

inventory.title: Queue supply is the hard problem
inventory.hook: A social calendar is easy to draw. Keeping it supplied is harder.
inventory.body: I care about turning real source material into reusable publishing inventory, not starting from a blank prompt every morning.
inventory.cta: What keeps your content queue empty?

inventory.title: Publishing needs destination truth
inventory.hook: Publishing is not just text plus a date.
inventory.body: The useful system also knows which account was authorised, what payload was reserved, what consequence happened and what is safe to retry.
inventory.cta: Which publishing state do your tools hide from you?

proof-and-state.label: Proof & State
proof-and-state.event_problem: The portfolio problem is preserving authority, evidence and product boundaries without allowing an executor or verifier to certify itself.
proof-and-state.event_cta: Where does your AI-work handover lose authority or evidence context?
proof-and-state.claim_boundary: Portfolio governance and evidence-boundary framing only; no claim that every portfolio product or deployment is currently available.
proof-and-state.default_cta: Where does your AI-work handover lose authority or evidence context?

inventory.title: Execution and verification should stay separate
inventory.hook: The system that did the work should not be the only system saying it succeeded.
inventory.body: Proof & State keeps execution, independent verification and evidence indexing as separate responsibilities so one product cannot silently certify itself.
inventory.cta: Where does self-certification creep into your AI workflow?

inventory.title: Authority needs a durable handover
inventory.hook: An AI handover is weak if the next person has to reconstruct who was allowed to do what.
inventory.body: The useful record keeps authority, exact state, evidence references and remaining decisions together instead of depending on chat history.
inventory.cta: Which handover fact do you most often have to reconstruct?

inventory.title: Trust domains should not collapse
inventory.hook: Fast automation gets dangerous when every trust role collapses into one process.
inventory.body: Execution, observation and evidence can cooperate without becoming the same authority. That separation makes later review more meaningful.
inventory.cta: Which trust role is currently doing too much in your stack?

donestate.label: DoneState
donestate.event_problem: The product problem is letting an agent execute bounded repository work without turning model judgement into authority or completion proof.
donestate.event_cta: What repository task would you delegate if the authority boundary and completion evidence were explicit?
donestate.claim_boundary: Authorised execution and durable-state framing only; no self-verification, merge, deployment, or general production-fleet authority claim.
donestate.default_cta: What repository task would you delegate if the authority boundary and completion evidence were explicit?

inventory.title: Delegate the outcome, not every tool call
inventory.hook: Supervising every agent command is not the same as governing the outcome.
inventory.body: DoneState lets the human define an objective and authority envelope while the harness chooses implementation steps inside that boundary.
inventory.cta: Which coding task still needs too much command-by-command supervision?

inventory.title: Done is not verified
inventory.hook: A successful command is not a completion proof.
inventory.body: DoneState keeps execution state separate from independent verification and stops at the handoff boundary until an external verifier attests the exact result.
inventory.cta: What evidence would you require before accepting an agent task as complete?

inventory.title: Ambiguous effects should stop
inventory.hook: The dangerous retry is the one after you do not know whether the first effect happened.
inventory.body: DoneState treats uncertain consequential effects as AMBIGUOUS_EFFECT instead of blindly replaying them.
inventory.cta: Which agent action would you never want retried blindly?

parcelbasis.label: Tax Lien Intelligence
required_phrases_any: county parcel and tax lien data
parcelbasis.event_problem: The customer problem is turning messy county data into a reviewable decision trail rather than another opaque score.
parcelbasis.event_cta: Which part of county-list review consumes the most time?
parcelbasis.claim_boundary: Decision-support workflow only; no investment-return or legal/tax outcome claim.
parcelbasis.default_cta: Which part of county-list review consumes the most time?

inventory.title: A shortlist needs reasons
inventory.hook: A ranked parcel list is not yet a decision record.
inventory.body: The useful workflow keeps the evidence, scoring reasons, comparison state and the decision history together so a later review can explain why an item moved forward.
inventory.cta: What do you currently have to reconstruct by hand?

inventory.title: County data needs repair before ranking
inventory.hook: Bad county data does not become trustworthy because you sorted it.
inventory.body: Import mapping, repair and explainable scoring matter because the review is only as useful as the evidence that survived ingestion.
inventory.cta: Where does your current county-data workflow break first?

inventory.title: Watchlists need decision context
inventory.hook: A watchlist without decision context becomes another pile of names.
inventory.body: The durable value is knowing what changed, why the item is still interesting, and what review step comes next.
inventory.cta: What context disappears from your watchlist today?

agentproof.label: AgentProof
agentproof.event_problem: The problem is giving consequential agent actions a verifiable authority and receipt trail.
agentproof.event_cta: What agent action would you refuse to trust without a receipt?
agentproof.claim_boundary: Release-candidate and source-consumption framing only; no hosted production authority claim.
agentproof.default_cta: What agent action would you refuse to trust without a receipt?

inventory.title: Success needs a receipt
inventory.hook: An agent saying ‘done’ is not the same as proving what happened.
inventory.body: For consequential repository changes I want the prepared state, approval, execution and signed receipt to remain independently checkable afterwards.
inventory.cta: What would you want in the receipt?

inventory.title: Authority should be explicit
inventory.hook: The executor should not quietly become the approval authority.
inventory.body: Keeping proposer, approver, executor, signer and verifier distinct makes the trust boundary inspectable instead of implied.
inventory.cta: Where does authority blur in your agent workflow?

inventory.title: Exactly-once matters
inventory.hook: Retries are where safe automation gets interesting.
inventory.body: A consequential agent action needs a way to distinguish a safe repeat from a second mutation after an uncertain first attempt.
inventory.cta: Which retry path worries you most?

global-bill-forge.label: Global Bill Forge
global-bill-forge.claim_boundary: International invoicing problem framing; do not repeat old production-ready wording without deployment proof.
global-bill-forge.default_cta: Which international invoicing edge case costs you the most manual work?

inventory.title: Currency is not just a symbol
inventory.hook: Changing £ to $ is not international invoicing.
inventory.body: Locale formatting, numbering systems, payment details and paper conventions can change the document too.
inventory.cta: Which international format catches you out most often?

inventory.title: RTL changes the document
inventory.hook: A global invoice has to work when the reading direction changes too.
inventory.body: RTL/LTR layout support is a document problem, not a cosmetic afterthought when the customer operates in a different script.
inventory.cta: Do you currently rebuild documents for RTL customers?

inventory.title: Payment detail varies by market
inventory.hook: The payment block is part of the invoice contract.
inventory.body: Bank transfer, routing, mobile-wallet and regional payment details do not fit one universal field set.
inventory.cta: Which payment detail do your templates handle badly?

openclaw-operator.label: OpenClaw Operator
openclaw-operator.event_problem: The product direction is bounded specialist operational work behind OpenClaw, with approvals and durable state where it matters.
openclaw-operator.event_cta: Which specialist workflow do you still supervise manually?
openclaw-operator.claim_boundary: OpenClaw remains the front door; this is specialist orchestration, not a replacement generic shell.
openclaw-operator.default_cta: Which specialist workflow do you still supervise manually?

inventory.title: Specialist lanes need state
inventory.hook: A general agent shell is not the same as a governed specialist workflow.
inventory.body: For operational work I want approvals, run history, incidents and bounded specialist state behind the front door.
inventory.cta: Which specialist lane would you delegate first?

inventory.title: OpenClaw can stay the front door
inventory.hook: The answer is not another generic dashboard.
inventory.body: OpenClaw can handle the general shell while the Operator layer focuses on specialist orchestration that needs stronger state and auditability.
inventory.cta: Where do you need more than a generic chat surface?

inventory.title: Handover should survive the chat
inventory.hook: Operational agent work should still make sense after the chat scrolls away.
inventory.body: Runs, approvals and incidents are useful because they preserve what happened independently of the conversation that triggered it.
inventory.cta: What state do you lose when an agent session ends?

agrolink-nigeria.label: AgroLink Nigeria
agrolink-nigeria.claim_boundary: Discovery/problem framing only; broad README feature list is not treated as verified live capability.
agrolink-nigeria.default_cta: Which step creates the most friction in Nigerian raw-material trade?

inventory.title: Listings are only the start
inventory.hook: A supplier listing does not complete a raw-material trade.
inventory.body: Buyers still need confidence around quality, terms, logistics and follow-through before a marketplace becomes operationally useful.
inventory.cta: Which part of the trade still happens off-platform for you?

inventory.title: Trust is part of marketplace design
inventory.hook: Marketplace liquidity is not enough if counterparties cannot evaluate trust.
inventory.body: Quality evidence and clear commercial terms are part of the transaction workflow, not just catalogue metadata.
inventory.cta: What proof do buyers ask you for before they move?

inventory.title: Cross-border trade adds coordination cost
inventory.hook: Cross-border raw-material trade is a coordination problem as much as a discovery problem.
inventory.body: Language, currency, logistics and documentation all add friction after buyer and supplier find each other.
inventory.cta: Which coordination step causes the longest delay?

agent-shop-products.label: Agent Shop Products
agent-shop-products.event_problem: The product question is when a reusable agent workflow deserves a versioned product boundary instead of living in old chats.
agent-shop-products.event_cta: What workflow have you reused enough times that it should become a product?
agent-shop-products.claim_boundary: Current source-backed catalogue only; no future commerce or premium inventory claim.
agent-shop-products.default_cta: What workflow have you reused enough times that it should become a product?

inventory.title: Reusable workflows deserve versioning
inventory.hook: If you keep reusing an agent workflow, it starts behaving like a product.
inventory.body: Versioned source, catalogue metadata and explicit evidence boundaries make it easier to inspect and improve than a prompt buried in chat history.
inventory.cta: Which workflow have you copied more than three times?

inventory.title: Catalogue metadata is not the payload
inventory.hook: A product catalogue should not require publishing every underlying payload.
inventory.body: Separating public metadata from the source product itself gives discovery a clean boundary without pretending the whole commerce layer already exists.
inventory.cta: What metadata would you need before trying an agent product?

inventory.title: No mock inventory
inventory.hook: A shop full of placeholder agent products teaches you nothing about demand.
inventory.body: I would rather keep the catalogue source-backed and small than manufacture inventory that has no real workflow behind it.
inventory.cta: Would you rather see fewer real workflows or a bigger synthetic catalogue?

opstruth.label: OpsTruth
opstruth.event_problem: The product problem is separating verified evidence, skipped checks and unknowns instead of turning absence into confidence.
opstruth.event_cta: What part of your AI-assisted build are you least sure was actually verified?
opstruth.claim_boundary: Read-only verification framing; no mutation authority or blanket production-readiness claim.
opstruth.default_cta: What part of your AI-assisted build are you least sure was actually verified?

inventory.title: Unknown should stay unknown
inventory.hook: Missing evidence should not become a green check.
inventory.body: A useful engineering verifier keeps failed, skipped, not-configured and not-verified states distinct so the report tells you what still needs proof.
inventory.cta: Which missing check gets mistaken for success in your stack?

inventory.title: Read-only is a feature
inventory.hook: A verifier does not need mutation authority to tell you what it can prove.
inventory.body: Keeping the checking layer read-only makes the evidence boundary easier to inspect and limits what a diagnostic tool can accidentally change.
inventory.cta: Would you give your verifier write access?

inventory.title: Confidence needs scope
inventory.hook: Checks passed is incomplete without saying which checks ran.
inventory.body: Confidence becomes more useful when the report also names runtime, route or production evidence that was never observed.
inventory.cta: What does your current CI report leave unproven?

capability-intelligence.label: Capability Intelligence
capability-intelligence.event_problem: The product problem is helping an agent distinguish discoverable capability from something it is actually authorised and ready to use.
capability-intelligence.event_cta: Which capability state causes the most confusion in your stack?
capability-intelligence.claim_boundary: Read-only capability discovery and decision support; no automatic installation or execution claim.
capability-intelligence.default_cta: Which capability state causes the most confusion in your stack?

inventory.title: Installed is not runnable
inventory.hook: Installed is not the same as runnable.
inventory.body: Capability Intelligence keeps discovered, present, installed, enabled, authenticated, runnable and verified separate instead of flattening them into one checkbox.
inventory.cta: Which lifecycle state does your tooling collapse?

inventory.title: Authority belongs in recommendations
inventory.hook: A useful tool recommendation should include the authority it would require.
inventory.body: The best candidate is not always the most powerful one; lower-authority, better-matched capabilities can be the safer decision.
inventory.cta: Do your agents explain the authority cost of the tool they pick?

inventory.title: Unknown is a valid lifecycle state
inventory.hook: Unknown is a better answer than invented readiness.
inventory.body: A cached schema does not prove authentication, and an installed plugin does not prove it is enabled or verified.
inventory.cta: Where does your stack guess instead of saying unknown?

tail-wagging-websites.label: Tail Wagging Websites
required_phrases_any: pet care business web design services
tail-wagging-websites.claim_boundary: Direct service/problem framing from current service list; no blanket security or guaranteed-growth claim.
tail-wagging-websites.default_cta: Where do pet-care customers drop out of your website journey?

inventory.title: Pretty is not enough
inventory.hook: A pet-care website is not doing its job just because it looks good.
inventory.body: The useful path connects local search, clear service pages, easy enquiry, follow-up automation and ongoing care.
inventory.cta: If your site gets traffic but not enquiries, where do people drop off?

inventory.title: Local SEO and conversion belong together
inventory.hook: Ranking locally is only half the job if the visitor still cannot decide what to do next.
inventory.body: Service-page clarity and enquiry flow matter because traffic only becomes useful when the next step is obvious.
inventory.cta: Which page on your pet-care site gets traffic but weak enquiries?

inventory.title: Website care is operational
inventory.hook: A website is not finished the day it launches.
inventory.body: Content, forms, automations, speed and maintenance keep changing after the first version, especially for a local service business.
inventory.cta: What part of your site has quietly gone stale?
